papers.title: An fMRI Investigation of Emotional Engagement in Moral Judgment
papers.authors: Greene, J. D., Sommerville, R. B., Nystrom, L. E., Darley, J. M., & Cohen, J. D.
papers.abstract_snippet: Seminal fMRI study showing that personal moral dilemmas (e.g., footbridge) engage emotional processing regions more than impersonal dilemmas (e.g., switch), establishing the neural dual-process framework for moral judgment.

papers.title: The Neural Bases of Cognitive Conflict and Control in Moral Judgment
papers.authors: Greene, J. D., Nystrom, L. E., Engell, A. D., Darley, J. M., & Cohen, J. D.
papers.abstract_snippet: Follow-up fMRI study demonstrating that utilitarian judgments in high-conflict moral dilemmas involve anterior cingulate cortex and dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, supporting cognitive control over emotional responses.

papers.title: The Cognitive Neuroscience of Moral Judgment
papers.abstract_snippet: Comprehensive chapter reviewing the cognitive neuroscience of moral judgment, synthesizing dual-process evidence from neuroimaging and behavioral studies. Argues moral judgments arise from competing neural systems.

papers.title: Beyond Point-and-Shoot Morality: Why Cognitive (Neuro)Science Matters for Ethics
papers.abstract_snippet: Argues that cognitive neuroscience evidence about moral judgment has normative implications. Defends deep pragmatism: understanding the dual-process mechanisms behind deontological intuitions should make us less trusting of them.

papers.title: Deontological and Utilitarian Inclinations in Moral Decision Making: A Process Dissociation Approach
papers.venue: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
papers.abstract_snippet: Introduces process dissociation procedure to independently measure deontological and utilitarian inclinations in moral dilemma responses, showing these are distinct processes rather than opposite ends of a single continuum.

papers.title: Action, Outcome, and Value: A Dual-System Framework for Morality
papers.abstract_snippet: Proposes a dual-system framework distinguishing action-based moral evaluation (model-free reinforcement learning) from outcome-based evaluation (model-based planning), integrating moral psychology with computational learning theory.

papers.title: Cognitive Load Selectively Interferes with Utilitarian Moral Judgment
papers.authors: Greene, J. D., Morelli, S. A., Lowenberg, K., Nystrom, L. E., & Cohen, J. D.
papers.abstract_snippet: Demonstrates that cognitive load selectively impairs utilitarian but not deontological moral judgments, providing behavioral evidence for the dual-process model where utilitarian judgments require more cognitive control.

papers.title: Large language models show amplified cognitive biases in moral decision-making
papers.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
papers.abstract_snippet: Shows that LLMs exhibit amplified versions of known human cognitive biases in moral decision-making scenarios, with implications for using AI systems in morally-loaded contexts.

papers.title: The Dual-Process Model and Moral Dilemmas
papers.abstract_snippet: Philosophical analysis of the dual-process model as applied to moral dilemmas, examining the normative implications of the distinction between intuitive and deliberative moral cognition.

papers.title: The Intuitive Greater Good: Testing the corrective dual process model of moral cognition
papers.abstract_snippet: Challenges the standard dual-process model by showing that utilitarian responses can also be intuitive, not just the product of deliberate cognitive override. Tests and revises the corrective dual process account.

papers.title: The neural basis of intuitive and counterintuitive moral judgment
papers.authors: Kahane, G., Wiech, K., Shackel, N., Farias, M., Savulescu, J., & Tracey, I.
papers.abstract_snippet: fMRI study investigating the neural correlates of intuitive versus counterintuitive moral judgments, showing distinct brain activation patterns that inform the dual-process debate in moral cognition.

papers.title: What makes moral dilemma judgments 'utilitarian' or 'deontological'?
papers.abstract_snippet: Examines what psychological processes underlie utilitarian and deontological responses in moral dilemmas, arguing that standard interpretations of trolley-type responses conflate distinct psychological mechanisms.

papers.title: LLM Ethics Benchmark: Three-Dimensional Assessment of Moral Reasoning in Large Language Models
papers.abstract_snippet: Proposes a three-dimensional framework for evaluating LLM ethical reasoning covering moral recognition, moral judgment, and moral action, with empirical evaluation across multiple LLMs.

papers.title: Structured Moral Reasoning in Language Models
papers.abstract_snippet: Evaluates structured moral reasoning capabilities in language models, analyzing how models decompose ethical problems and whether they follow principled reasoning chains.

papers.title: The Fragility of Moral Judgment in Large Language Models
papers.abstract_snippet: Demonstrates the fragility of moral judgments in LLMs under slight prompt variations, showing that models lack robust moral reasoning and are highly sensitive to surface-level changes in moral dilemma framing.
